// NEGATIVE fixture — `Object.hasOwn` only where a lexer must not see it. Nothing may be reported.
// A line comment: Object.hasOwn(obj, key)
/* A block comment: Object.hasOwn(obj, key) */
const SINGLE = 'Object.hasOwn(obj, key)';
const DOUBLE = "Object.hasOwn(obj, key)";
const TEMPLATE = `hasOwnProperty.call is the floor-safe form, never Object.hasOwn(obj, key)`;
const IN_REGEX = /Object\.hasOwn\b/;

export function mentionsHasOwn(source) {
  return /Object\.hasOwn\b/.test(source);
}

export function has(obj, key) {
  // Near-miss in real code: `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` is not `Object.hasOwn`.
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key);
}

export { SINGLE, DOUBLE, TEMPLATE, IN_REGEX };
